method.label: Bound the length using the sum formula

annotationRationale: The arithmetic-series formula produces an integer product equal to 90. Its positive integer factors bound the length, and an explicit sequence attains the bound.
sourceMethod: Follows the official alternative using the arithmetic-series formula and n(2a+n-1)=90, clarifying why the second factor is at least 1 and verifying the attaining sequence.

review.mathCheck: The sum gives \(n(2a+n-1)=90\). Its second factor is a positive integer, so \(n\le90\). Integers from \(-44\) through \(45\) attain 90 terms with sum 45. Choice D is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of the algebraic alternative in MAA 10A Solution 5, printed pages 2 and 3. It explicitly supplies the positivity argument behind the official bound.
review.annotationCheck: The bound and endpoint construction are fully explained. Finding every integer solution is unnecessary for the requested maximum.
